entries.title: Acute Limb Ischemia

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly names acute limb ischemia, pulse/Doppler assessment, timely referral, and revascularization, but is framed around traumatic vascular injury rather than the full non-traumatic acute limb ischemia topic.

testable_competencies.initial_action: Perform a focused vascular examination, arrange appropriate initial assessment, stabilize, and obtain urgent vascular consultation.

do_not_test: definitive open or endovascular revascularization technique

entries.title: Peripheral Arterial Disease and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize symptomatic peripheral arterial disease, ischemic wounds, and chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Perform a basic vascular examination, use initial non-invasive investigation appropriately, address risk factors, and identify when urgent vascular assessment is needed.

entries.uncertain_reason: Targeted canonical MCC searches for peripheral arterial disease and limb ischemia located no dedicated objective. This clinically important undergraduate-level recognition unit is retained without invented MCC evidence pending registry expansion or future human scope review.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Shock objective explicitly includes aortic dissection/obstruction among obstructive causes and requires recognition of urgency, critical investigation, tissue-perfusion support, and initial cause-directed management; it supports the emergency presentation rather than detailed dissection classification.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a presentation concerning for aortic dissection and major ischemic or rupture complications.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Initiate stabilization and urgent specialist/emergency escalation.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Shock objective supports recognition and immediate management of hemodynamic compromise from aortic obstruction or related acute vascular catastrophe, but it does not name aneurysm or support elective aneurysm surveillance and intervention decisions.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize aneurysm presentations that suggest rupture or other emergency complication.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Stabilize an unstable patient and obtain urgent vascular/surgical assessment.

entries.title: Carotid Stenosis

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: MCC Objectives, Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke), February 2017
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This objective explicitly supports assessment of acute neurologic deficits, bruits and risk factors, appropriate investigation, action, prevention, and acute or chronic medical/surgical intervention in the stroke/TIA context.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize carotid disease in the TIA/stroke risk context and perform an appropriate focused examination.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Arrange appropriate initial investigation, risk reduction, and urgent referral when neurologic symptoms are present.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Stroke/TIA assessment overlaps Neurology; no ownership decision is made at chapter scope stage.

entries.title: Venous Thromboembolism

mcc_evidence.official_source: MCC Objectives, Prevention of venous thrombosis, January 2017
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective directly supports risk assessment, examination, appropriate investigation, initial prevention measures, and anticoagulation, but its explicit focus is prevention rather than comprehensive DVT/PE diagnosis and treatment.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize venous thrombosis risk and vascular-context presentations requiring assessment.
testable_competencies.initial_action: Use appropriate initial investigation, prevention, escalation, and referral principles.

entries.cross_discipline_note: VTE overlaps Medicine, Hematology, and Emergency Medicine; no ownership decision is made at chapter scope stage.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize chronic venous disease features and complications such as venous ulceration, and distinguish them from ischemic-wound context.
Recognize the clinical features of lymphedema and identify when alternative or urgent causes of limb swelling require evaluation.
